blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Objective: Trofinetide, approved in 2023 as the first Rett syndrome treatment, lacks scalable real-world monitoring because chart review is labor-intensive. We developed a dual large language model (LLM) consensus pipeline to extract 18 treatment-response phenotypes, comprising 4 adverse effects, 13 Rett clinical features, and medication refusal, from clinical notes. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 26,763 notes from 108 patients with confirmed sustained trofinetide exposure at Texas Children's Hospital. The pipeline filters notes by keyword, classifies each through two LLMs requiring consensus, and aggregates a patient-by-timepoint matrix. Architecture and prompt were selected on a diarrhea development set, then frozen and applied to the other 17 phenotypes with the phenotype definition substituted, as an out-of-sample test. The reported prompt comparison scores 183 expert-labeled cells. Results: A prompt requiring diarrhea to be active and severe performed best (84.2 $\pm$ 0.0% accuracy; F1 = 0.674), 47 percentage points above regular-expression matching ($p < 0.0001$). Expert reviewers judged six of the pipeline's calls per phenotype, three positive and three negative, and agreed with 90.2% (92/102). The 13 Rett clinical features are manifestations of the disorder itself rather than adverse effects of trofinetide. Gross and fine motor impairment, language/communication, and stereotypy were documented present in 92-100% of patients at every visit. Discussion: In-context LLM extraction captured multi-domain treatment responses. The outcome is documented presence at each visit, not a direction-of-change judgment. Conclusion: Coupling in-context LLM reasoning with a consensus architecture offers a scalable alternative to keyword and regular-expression extraction for real-world evidence, adapting to new phenotypes and medications through configuration alone.

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Rett syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder affecting approximately
1 in 10,000–15,000 live female births, caused primarily by loss-of-function
mutations in the MECP2 gene [ 1 , 2 ] .
The condition is characterized by an initial period of apparently normal
development followed by a period of regression, with loss of acquired hand
skills, development of stereotypic hand movements, gait abnormalities, and
loss of spoken language [ 2 ] , followed by a period of
stabilization without further regression of skills.

of treatment-relevant phenotypes over 12 weeks, and real-world treatment
response across the full spectrum of Rett syndrome features remains
incompletely characterized.

blocks.en: Background and Significance
blocks.zh: 背景和意义

blocks.en:
Monitoring treatment response in Rett syndrome is challenging. The condition
manifests across multiple domains, including motor, cognitive, behavioral and
autonomic function, each potentially documented by a different specialist in
narrative notes. Manual chart review of the resulting note volume can
quickly become prohibitively labor-intensive. Electronic health record (EHR) phenotyping has therefore
turned to automated methods,
from concept-extraction systems [ 6 , 7 ] to
rule-based and portable phenotype algorithms [ 8 , 9 ] .
But traditional rule-based natural language processing
(NLP) [ 10 , 11 ] struggles to distinguish
active symptoms from historical, anticipatory, and negated mentions within
complex narratives [ 12 , 13 ] , a difficulty
long noted in adverse-event detection [ 14 , 15 ] .

blocks.en:
Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on clinical text and medical
benchmarks [ 16 , 17 , 18 , 19 ] ,
offering the contextual reasoning to interpret narratives, but a single LLM
applied directly to clinical extraction can perform poorly [ 20 ] .
In our data, a single model produced both false positives, over-interpreting
routine documentation, and false negatives. The appropriate architecture
depends on task complexity. Simple extraction tasks may suit a single
well-prompted model [ 21 , 22 ] .
Our task spans many phenotypes and requires judging, within each note, whether a
finding is active at that visit rather than historical, negated or anticipatory, so it
is complex enough to benefit from a multi-agent verification
design in which one model evaluates or critiques another’s
output [ 23 , 24 ] . We therefore use two
independently prompted models and require agreement before making a
positive call, prioritizing precision over recall.

blocks.en:
We present a dual-LLM consensus pipeline that extracts 18 treatment-response
phenotypes from clinical notes of 108 patients with Rett syndrome receiving
trofinetide.
The 18 comprise 4 adverse effects, 13 Rett clinical features and medication
refusal, and each is classified at every visit as documented present or absent
(Methods). The
pipeline was developed and evaluated on an expert-annotated ground truth for
the diarrhea phenotype, then applied to the remaining 17 phenotypes with only the
phenotype definition substituted.
Our objective was to
determine whether contextual LLM reasoning, combined with a consensus
requirement, can extract multi-domain treatment-response phenotypes from
routine clinical documentation at a scale that manual review cannot reach. We
focused on one major adverse effect, diarrhea, to develop the pipeline, and we
report that process in full.

blocks.en:
We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients with Rett syndrome
identified from Rett Center clinical visits at Texas Children’s Hospital (TCH)
who were prescribed or considered for trofinetide (Daybue). We selected this
population because the TCH Rett Center is a dedicated center of excellence whose
standardized note templates capture comprehensive disorder-specific information
over office visits of at least one hour.
An initial 115 patients were identified on this basis. To verify sustained
drug exposure,
an independent quality-control (QC) review triangulated three sources per
patient: pharmacy orders, medication-administration records, and longitudinal
note mentions. This confirmed sustained exposure in 108 of 115 patients
(94%) , with 65 by pharmacy order and 43 by clinical documentation alone
( ≥ \geq 2 note mentions over > > 60 days). The remaining 7 were unconfirmed (4
with only isolated mentions, 3 with no evidence) and were therefore excluded. This 108-patient QC-confirmed cohort is the analysis cohort throughout .

Center clinical team of two pediatric nurses and two pediatric neurologists,
who together performed all clinical annotation and review reported here, and
the notes and medication tables are drawn from the institutional EHR.

blocks.en:
Each keyword-positive note is independently classified by two LLMs with
complementary perspectives. The first, a clinical NLP expert, judges whether the
phenotype is documented in the note itself, applying explicit rules to separate
findings recorded at that visit from historical, negated, anticipatory, and
template mentions against a written per-phenotype definition. For diarrhea that
definition adds a severity threshold. The second, a domain specialist (gastroenterologist for side
effects, pediatric neurologist for the Rett clinical features), weighs clinical
significance and attribution. Prompt templates, YES/NO criteria, and a contingency table of the two
agents’ calls (evidence they work independently) are in Supplementary
Notes S3 and S1. Both output a
structured YES/NO call with supporting evidence, and a note is positive only
when both models agree YES. The record also carries the note’s contact date, which
is known from EHR metadata rather than extracted from the note text (Supplementary
Note S3). The evidence spans were spot-checked but not systematically validated. Detection is thus note-local in time , so
historical mentions score negative, at the cost of missing purely retrospective
ones (quantified in the error analysis).

Documented rates vary across the adverse effects (Figure 3 A).
Other side effects are documented in 11% of patients at baseline and rise
sharply to 58% at 6 months, settling at 38–49% thereafter. Medication refusal

concern. Vomiting fluctuates modestly, peaking at 38% at 12 months and falling
to 22% by 30 months. Diarrhea,
the only validated adverse effect, is characterized separately
(Figure 2 ).

blocks.en:
These 13 features are manifestations of Rett syndrome itself and not adverse
effects of trofinetide, so their documented presence describes the disorder
under treatment rather than harm caused by it. They span a wide range of
documented prevalence
(Figure 3 A; full rates in Supplementary Table S8). Gross- and
fine-motor impairment, impaired language/communication, and hand stereotypies are
the core neurodevelopmental features of the disorder, and all are documented as
present in nearly all patients at every visit (92–100%).
Dysautonomia, breathing, bruxism, sleep, and seizure form a middle band at
intermediate rates, while attention/alertness, anxiety, and the affective and
behavioral findings of mood and aggression are documented least often.
Documented presence at the pre-treatment baseline is lower than at 6 months for
5 of the 13 features, so baseline-to-follow-up differences should still not be
read as clinical change (Supplementary Table S8). These
trajectories are documentation-based and, except for diarrhea, are not
validated against a ground truth (Discussion).

We classified every diarrhea discrepancy under the reported configuration (29 of
183 cells) by root cause (Table 4 ,
Figure 2 D), assigning each cell by rule from the
keyword-passing notes in its own window and the adjacent ones rather than by
manual re-reading. Three mechanisms account for all 29, and all three are
annotation, data-coverage, or window-placement limitations rather than
demonstrable misreadings. The reviewer integrates patient-level context
across encounters and grades case by case, while the model is note-local by
construction and applies one fixed threshold uniformly.

blocks.en: Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论情况

blocks.en:
A dual-LLM consensus pipeline can extract clinically meaningful
treatment-response phenotypes from unstructured notes at scale, recovering signal
that structured fields miss. Modeling clinical context significantly outperforms
naive keyword matching, and what separates the configurations that do so is what
the prompt counts as diarrhea rather than how many models are asked. The
severe-diarrhea prompt was strongest, but its margin over the deployed prompt is
unresolved at this sample size, so we adopt it as a precision-favorable default
rather than a proven improvement. It was also selected on the same 183 cells it is
scored on, so its accuracy is an in-sample upper bound. The evidence that the
design transfers is the half-cohort split and the 90.2% agreement on the other 17
phenotypes, which the same architecture and prompt design reached with only the
phenotype definition substituted.

blocks.en:
The main limitation is that only diarrhea has a ground truth. The other 17
phenotypes rest on spot-check review and inter-LLM agreement rather than full
annotation (Supplementary Note S1), a resource constraint described in Methods.
Their rates are therefore hypothesis-generating lower bounds, and generalization
likely varies by phenotype, since concrete adverse effects should transfer more
readily than subjective findings. The pipeline detects only what our corpus documents, and some
symptoms surface only in other channels. The exposure anchor is adjudicated from
note text for most patients rather than taken from a structured record, so window
boundaries carry real uncertainty, visible in the 12 displacement errors. The observed trajectories cannot be definitively
attributed to trofinetide rather than to concurrent therapies or the natural
course of development. The outcome is documented presence and not direction of
change or severity, so the pipeline cannot distinguish an improved feature from a
persistent one. For the core Rett features, documented in nearly all patients at
nearly every visit, detecting within-feature improvement would need
severity-graded instruments such as the RSBQ or CGI-I. Documentation does move for
other side effects and refusing medication, so the method registers change when
change is recorded. All patients come from a single institution, and the pipeline
is not yet optimized for efficiency, which cheap pre-filtering, batched calls, and
smaller distilled models could improve.

blocks.en:
Integrating additional sources such as telephone logs and portal messages, and
cross-temporal reasoning that propagates retrospective mentions to the timepoint
they describe, would recover symptoms currently missed. Expanding the ground truth
by second-reviewer adjudication and by annotation prioritized on inter-LLM
disagreement would convert the six-case agreement tiers into per-phenotype
accuracy with confidence intervals. Individual feature trajectories, including the
apparent seizure rise, need validated per-timepoint annotation before clinical
interpretation and are deferred. Direction-of-change extraction is feasible in the
same architecture with phenotype-specific prompts and a correspondingly annotated
ground truth, but was outside this validation’s scope. The framework extends to
other medications and conditions by configuration alone.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en:
We present a dual-LLM consensus pipeline for multi-phenotype treatment-response
extraction from clinical notes, applied to 108 patients with Rett syndrome receiving
trofinetide over 30 months. Using Claude Opus 4.6, it substantially outperforms
a regular-expression baseline on an expert-annotated diarrhea development set, and the
same configuration transfers out-of-sample to the remaining 17 phenotypes with only
the phenotype definition substituted.
It also yields one of the first comprehensive real-world characterizations of
how multi-domain trofinetide response is documented in routine care. The architecture extends to further
phenotypes, medications, and institutions by configuration alone, showing that
LLM consensus can bridge clinical narrative and the structured data needed for
scalable treatment-response monitoring and real-world evidence in rare
diseases.

blocks.en:
Because only diarrhea has an expert ground truth, we also measured the agreement
between the two independently prompted agents, which requires no labels. Cohen’s κ \kappa between LLM 1 (clinical NLP expert) and LLM 2 (GI/neurology specialist)
was computed over the 60,530 note–phenotype instances that both models
classified (Figure S1 A). Overall agreement was high
( κ = 0.930 \kappa=0.930 , raw agreement 96.6%), and all 17 phenotypes reached κ ≥ 0.73 \kappa\geq 0.73 , with per-phenotype values in Table S3 . Seven
of the 60,537 matches did not return a valid YES or NO from both models and were
scored negative. Because the two prompts were written independently, their
agreement is a proxy for how well specified a phenotype is. It does not track the
per-phenotype expert agreement from the spot-check, however. Attention/alertness has
the lowest κ \kappa (0.732) yet reached 6/6 on review, while dysautonomia
( κ = 0.917 \kappa=0.917 ) and refusing medication ( κ = 0.890 \kappa=0.890 ) reached only 4/6. With six
cases per phenotype the spot-check cannot resolve differences of that size, so the two
signals should be read as independent rather than concordant.

Prompt V2’s accuracy in main-text Table 2 carries an SD of 0.0 because its
confusion matrix is identical in all three runs, at 30 true positives,
124 true negatives, 12 false positives and 17 false negatives. This is a property
of the aggregation step and not evidence that the prompt is deterministic. At the
note level the consensus call does move, flipping on 7, 9 and 8 of the 2,260
classified notes across the three run pairs, and on 3, 4 and 3 of the 1,404
notes that fall inside the annotated patients’ evaluation windows. None of those
flips changes a cell. Aggregation marks a patient–timepoint Yes if any note in the six-month bucket receives a positive call, so a flip on a
note whose bucket already holds another positive is absorbed. The deployed
prompt V0 flips on 15, 11 and 10 notes over the same pairs, and one of its cells
does move. The zero is therefore correct arithmetic at the cell level while the
underlying note-level classification remains stochastic, and it should not be
read as prompt stability.

blocks.en:
No seed and no sampling parameters were set in any of the 42 model-invocation
nodes, so temperature, top- p p , top- k k and the token limit took platform
defaults throughout, as the main-text Methods states. The three runs are
therefore independent draws rather than replays of a single run. We verified this
on the response strings themselves, since the platform exposes no per-call
telemetry. Under V2, Agent 1 returned byte-identical text on 2,243 of the
2,260 notes and Agent 2 on 2,251, whereas a cached or memoized path would
return identical strings everywhere. Byte differences outnumber label flips, so
part of the run-to-run variation is wording that leaves the YES/NO verdict
unchanged.

blocks.en:
This note expands the model-development summary in the main-text Methods. The
pipeline was reached through a sequence of designs, each built to address a
failure mode observed in the previous one, and the benchmark of the six retained
methods against the 189-cell diarrhea ground truth is in
Table S11 .

blocks.en:
Two points bound how those numbers relate to the main text. First, the
architecture was selected on the original note corpus, the order-date exposure
anchor and a 189-cell grid, and it is reported here on the numbers it was decided
with. The architecture it settled on was then held fixed, and the prompt
comparison in the main text varies the prompt instead, on the refreshed corpus and
the corrected anchor. The two sets of numbers are not interchangeable. Second, the negation-aware NLP row of main-text Table 2 is not the rule-based
NLP of Table S11 . It is a reimplementation written for the
rerun so that every method in Table 2 is scored on one grid, and it reaches
42.1% there against the 70.9% of rule-based NLP. The regular expression row
is the Stage 0 floor below, and matches its 42.3% on the original grid.

blocks.en:
The earliest approach flagged any note containing a diarrhea keyword. Recall is
high but precision is poor, because negated, historical, templated and
anticipatory mentions are all counted positive, as in “denies diarrhea,” “had
diarrhea last year,” checkbox review-of-systems fields and “call if diarrhea
develops.” Every subsequent design targets one of these false-positive sources.
blocks.zh:
最早的方法标出了含有痢疾关键词的任何注释. 记得
高但精度低,因为被否定、历史、模板和
预告性提到都是积极的,如“痢疾、”
去年的痢疾,”系统复议栏和“痢疾打电话
发展。” 之后的每一个设计都针对这些假阳性来源之一.

blocks.en:
We added regular-expression negation detection and temporal cue matching to
discount past-tense and resolved mentions. This substantially improved precision
over the floor but was brittle. Hand-written patterns missed paraphrases and
complex sentence structure, and over-aggressive negation occasionally suppressed
true positives.
blocks.zh:
我们加入了常规表达否定检测 和时间提示匹配到
折扣过去和解决的提及。 这种精度大大提高了
在地板上,但很柔软。 手写图案省略
复杂的句子结构,有时压制过度的否定
真正的阳性。

blocks.en:
We layered three further components onto the rule-based system. Clinical-form and
template filters remove boilerplate and blank-field matches, severity gates
down-weight “mild,” “controlled” and “resolving” language, and simple
cross-temporal handling was added. At equal overall accuracy to the rule-based model, this
recovered recall that the stricter negation rules had removed, so the two systems
sat at different points on the same precision–recall frontier rather than one
dominating the other.
blocks.zh:
我们把另外三个组件分解到基于规则的系统中。 临床形式和
模板过滤器去除锅炉板和空场匹配,重度门
减重的“混合”、“控制”和“溶解”语言,以及简单
增加了跨时空处理。 以与基于规则的模式相同的总体准确性,
重新回顾,更严格的否定规则已经取消,所以两种制度
在不同地点坐在一起 精确地回顾边界而不是一个
主宰彼众生.

blocks.en:
Before the full ground truth existed, we prototyped a three-pass LLM approach on a
32-patient subset to test whether contextual reasoning could move beyond the
rule-based frontier. It established feasibility but used a different evaluation
set with no paired ground truth, so it is not part of the six-method benchmark.

在完全真相存在之前,我们以三通LLM方法为原型

以规则为基础的边界。 它确立了可行性,但采用了不同的评价

blocks.en:
Once the full ground truth was available, we evaluated a single
clinical-NLP-expert LLM, whose accuracy (72.7%) edged above the rule-based
frontier (70.9%) although the difference was not resolved at 189 cells. Adding a
second, differently prompted domain-specialist model raised the question of how to
combine the two outputs. We tested both aggregation rules on identical model
outputs. An OR-gate ( permissive , positive if either agent says Yes)
maximizes sensitivity but readmits false positives, while an AND-gate
( consensus , positive only if both agree) favors precision. The consensus
gate gave the best overall accuracy and the most run-stable operating point, and
was adopted.

Having fixed the gate, we tried loosening what the prompt counts as a positive.
Both agents were instructed to score any documented diarrhea as present,
dropping the exclusion for diarrhea that was mild or already controlled with
medication, on the reasoning that a symptom under treatment is still a symptom.
This raised recall as intended but added far more false positives than it
recovered true ones, so overall accuracy fell well below the adopted design and
the change was reverted. Note S7 quantifies the same effect on the reported grid
as versions V1 and V4.

Table S11 , panel B, reports all 15 pairwise McNemar exact tests

significantly outperforms the regex floor ( p < 0.0001 p<0.0001 , and after Holm correction).
The comparisons above the floor are directionally consistent with the accuracy
ordering, with the consensus model winning each head-to-head disagreement, for
example 24 discordant cells to 14 against hybrid NLP, but none reaches
significance ( p = 0.11 p=0.11 – 1.0 1.0 ). This reflects limited power rather than an absence
of effect. The consensus-versus-NLP gap rests on a net of roughly ten cells of

blocks.en: Supplementary Note S4. Reading the Error Taxonomy, and Intended Use
blocks.zh: S4. 读取错误分类学和预期用途

blocks.en:
The taxonomy in main-text Table 4 covers the 29 errors of the reported
configuration. Two points about it are worth stating.

配置 值得指出两点。

blocks.en:
The taxonomy does not contain a category for the model misreading a note, and that
absence is a limit of the method rather than a finding. Each error was assigned by
rule, from where the supporting evidence sits relative to the scored window, so the
categories can separate a window-placement mismatch from a threshold disagreement
but cannot tell whether a note was misread within its own window. The prompts emit
only YES or NO, so nothing in the output records the reasoning behind a call.

what accuracy becomes if every threshold-disagreement cell is re-scored as correct
wherever the model and the note agree the symptom is present. Reaching it
defensibly would require re-adjudicating the ground truth prospectively, under a
severity threshold written into both the annotation guideline and the prompt,
rather than relabeling the current errors after the fact.

blocks.en:
The operating point we report, precision 0.714 and recall 0.638 on diarrhea, is
well suited to cohort-level inference and triage but not to autonomous
per-patient decision-making. At this precision and recall the pipeline is best used
to estimate phenotype prevalence and trajectories across a population, where over-
and under-calls partially offset in aggregate, and to surface candidate notes for a
human reviewer. Errors are also non-random, concentrating in threshold-ambiguous
cases, so any per-patient use should keep a clinician in the loop and treat a
positive call as a prompt for review rather than a conclusion. We therefore frame
the extracted rates as a real-world evidence and hypothesis-generation tool, and
the individual note classifications as a triage aid.

blocks.en: Supplementary Note S6. Annotation Procedure

blocks.en:
The diarrhea ground truth and the multi-phenotype expert spot-check were
established by the Rett Center clinical team, comprising two pediatric nurses
familiar with the Rett syndrome clinic and two pediatric neurologists, who worked
as a single reviewing group throughout. For each patient and timepoint window the
reviewers examined the available clinical notes and labeled the cell Yes for
medication-associated diarrhea, No, or Deceased/Not applicable. Where diarrhea was
recorded, its severity was noted on the clinic’s four-level scale: 1, loose stool in
diaper; 2, watery stool in diaper; 3, watery stool on clothes; 4, watery stool
outside clothes. The operative question was
whether documented diarrhea represented a medication side effect as opposed to a
tolerated, controlled or pre-existing baseline symptom. This is the same judgment
that drives the reviewer–model threshold disagreements in main-text Table 4.

The reviewers resolved each cell together by consensus rather than annotating
independently against a written guideline. No formal written guideline was issued,

tighten the ground truth and allow the reviewer–model threshold disagreements to be
quantified rather than adjudicated case by case.

a note governs an earlier onset, and that a finding attributed to another cause is
absent. Version V0 is the deployed prompt and serves as the base case. Each version
was run three times. Table S10 reports the results, and three

blocks.en:
The prompt experiment leaves open the possibility that the single extraction
question asks for two judgments at once, whether diarrhea has started and whether it
is currently uncontrolled. We tested that reading by replacing the single question
with two simpler ones and combining them in code rather than in the prompt.
Variable A asks only whether diarrhea has begun as a side effect of trofinetide at
any point up to and including the visit. Variable B asks only whether it is
adequately controlled at the visit. The two were combined by a deterministic state
rule that labels diarrhea present from the visit at which onset is first detected
and absent from the visit at which control is first established. Ten combination
rules were evaluated, varying that rule, the direction of the consensus gate and the
within-window aggregation order, all at no additional inference cost, since each is
a function of the same two extracted variables.

blocks.en:

window boundaries (Note S8), but it cannot remove the lag between a symptom starting
and a note recording it. A third experiment asked what accuracy would be available

left the extraction untouched and slid each patient’s sequence of predicted visits so
that the first visit predicted positive falls at the first on-treatment visit, padding
the vacated tail as negative. Only the model output moves, so every cell remains
comparable against the same annotation. Applied to the deployed prompt’s modal
predictions this raised accuracy from 79.8% to 84.2%, the best F1 anywhere in the
family at 0.707 (variant S1 in Table S10 , panel C), matching
the reported prompt from the opposite direction, by cutting false negatives rather
than false positives.

cells, because 35 of the 47 positive cells sit at that one visit. Much of the

rather than by the content of the individual note, which is a property of this

blocks.en:
The results above are the final stage of an iterative process and not a set of
independent replications. We first searched over architectures, then over prompts,
running rounds of error analysis between stages and carrying the surviving
configuration forward each time. Two things changed along the way. Error analysis
showed that some of the remaining error was in the data rather than in the model, so
the note pull was extended from one ending in 2025 to one extending through August
2026, and the exposure anchor was replaced (Note S8). Earlier stages were therefore
run on a different corpus and a different set of evaluation windows, and their
numbers are not comparable to the ones reported here. Where an earlier stage and the
final run disagree, we report the final run.

blocks.en: Supplementary Note S8. The Exposure Anchor

blocks.en:
Every follow-up window is measured from the date trofinetide was started, so that
date determines which visit a note is scored against. The deployed pipeline took it
from the earliest trofinetide record in the Epic order table, and the resulting
windows disagreed with the expert annotation more often than the note content did.
Manual review of the record explained why. Trofinetide is an oral solution dispensed
by a specialty pharmacy and given at home, so the drug appears in orders, charts and
correspondence well before the family gives the first dose, and the order is followed
by pharmacy processing, insurance authorization and a four-week titration. In one
reviewed patient the prescription reached the specialty pharmacy 73 days after the
order, insurance declined coverage the same day, and the first record of the family
giving the drug is at day 114. In another the order preceded the first documented
dose by more than two years. In both cases the agents read every note correctly and
the error was in which window the note had been placed.

We therefore replaced the order date with the earliest documented exposure ,
taken in order of preference from the medication administration record, then from a
dispense or fill record, and otherwise from the earliest note adjudicated as
documenting active dosing. Of the 108 QC-confirmed patients, 8 anchor on an
administration record and 91 on an adjudicated note, while 9 have no reliable
evidence of a start date and are excluded from the timepoint analysis. None anchors
on a dispense record, because trofinetide fills go through a specialty pharmacy and
never reach the institutional dispense tables. The correction is large and does not
depend on the labels, moving the median patient by 116 days, with more than half
moving by more than 90 days. It also moves six
cells out of the follow-up range, taking the grid from 189 cells to 183 while
conserving the contributing patients and the 47 positive cells, and accuracy under

report the two grids side by side. Two negative controls confirm that the result does
not follow from displacing windows as such, since neither randomly re-anchoring the
patients nor permuting their timepoint labels reaches the observed accuracy in 200
draws.

blocks.en:
The corrected anchor does not remove the problem entirely. It cannot recover the lag
between a symptom starting and a note recording it, and the annotation is cell-level
and carries no dates, so a reviewer may place a symptom at the stage of treatment
where it clinically belongs rather than at the timestamp of the note that records it.
Both effects are visible in the gap between the two ways of scoring the pipeline.
Judged note by note, where the anchor plays no part, agreement with expert review is
about 90%, at 90.2% over the full 17-phenotype spot-check and 91.4% over the 58
of those cases that fall inside an evaluation window (Note S6). Judged cell by cell, where
every call must also land in the right six-month window, the reported configuration
reaches 84.2%. We read the difference as the cost of identifying the start date from
the record rather than as a failure to read the notes, which is why the residual
temporal errors in main-text Table 4 are the largest remaining category after
threshold disagreement.
